connections.title: Connections
connections.description: Agent providers, GitHub and MCP servers this project uses. Each agent profile chooses its connection and model.

editAgent.title: Edit {{connection}}
editAgent.description: What this connection’s CLI runs on: its own sign-in on an account, or an API provider. Its program stays as it is; rename it from its details in Connections.

menu.agentDetail: Codex CLI, Claude Code CLI, Anthropic API or OpenAI API
menu.mcpDetail: A program on this computer, or a remote server

notice.providers: Each agent can use a different provider. Choose the connection and model in each agent profile; one pipeline can mix providers.
notice.github: Pull requests and the Create pull request tool reach GitHub only through gh. Its accounts are shared by every project on this computer; {{project}} records the one it expects.
notice.mcp: Agents run without your own CLI configuration, so the MCP servers they get are the ones {{project}} adds here. Each agent profile chooses which of them its agents get.

connections.ownership: Connections belong to {{project}}. A CLI connection runs on one of your accounts, which every project shares; {{project}} records which account each connection runs on.
connections.emptyDetail: A connection is how {{project}} reaches an agent provider (a CLI on this computer or a model API with a project key), GitHub through gh, or an MCP server. Add the Codex or Claude Code CLI installed on this computer; each agent profile then chooses its connection and model.

detail.noAccount: This connection runs on no account, so runs on it don't start. Choose an account for it in Edit connection.
detail.notChecked: This connection has not been checked yet.
detail.connected: The CLI answers and its account is signed in. Orchester runs it with that account's folder.
detail.signInCodex: The Codex CLI is not signed in. Run codex login in a terminal, then check again. Orchester never signs in for you.
detail.signInClaude: The Claude Code CLI is not signed in. Run claude auth login in a terminal, then check again. Orchester never signs in for you.
detail.signInUnknown: The CLI answers, but whether it is signed in could not be determined. Agents may fail to start until it is.
detail.executableMissing: The program file does not exist. Install the CLI again, then check again.
detail.notRecognized: The program answered, but not as the expected CLI.
detail.couldNotRun: The program could not be started or did not answer in time. Check again.

connections.modelsAfterCheck: Models are known after a successful check.
connections.noModelsListed: The CLI listed no models. Profiles can still enter a model id, marked as not verified.

modelSource.provider: Listed by the model catalog bundled with the CLI.
modelSource.aliases: The CLI did not list its models; these are the current model ids and the aliases its help documents.
modelSource.providerAndCurrentIds: The current model ids, then the models the CLI lists.
modelSource.apiProvider: Typed for the API provider; Orchester does not check that it serves them.

cliTooOld.heading: {{cli}} {{installed}} can’t run {{model}}; version {{required}} or newer is needed
cliTooOld.detail: A run found this when the model’s provider refused the CLI. Update the CLI, then check the connection again.

connections.notUsed: No agent profile uses this connection yet.
connections.runInTerminal: Run this in a terminal, then check again.

result.checkingCli: Asking {{program}} for its version, sign-in and models. A question it doesn't answer within {{seconds}} seconds counts as no answer.
result.checkingGh: Asking gh for its version, account and scopes. A question it doesn't answer within {{seconds}} seconds counts as no answer.
result.unread: Test ran, but its result could not be read
result.verified: {{program}} {{version}} answers and is signed in. Models listed: {{models}}.
result.verifiedProvider: {{program}} {{version}} answers. It runs on the API provider, so its own sign-in is not used.
result.signedOut: {{program}} {{version}} answers, but it is not signed in.
result.signInUnknown: {{program}} {{version}} answers, but whether it is signed in could not be read.
result.keyMissing: {{program}} {{version}} answers, but the secret holding its API key is archived or gone.
result.notFound: The program file was not found.
result.notRecognized: The program answered, but not as {{program}}.
result.couldNotRun: The program did not start, or did not answer within {{seconds}} seconds.
result.githubSignedIn: gh answers and is signed in as {{account}}.

nativeNotAvailable.heading: {{connection}} uses {{provider}}, which is not available yet
nativeNotAvailable.detail: Native agents are not available in this version of Orchester. A step whose profile runs on this connection doesn’t start, so a run with one doesn’t start either. Choose a Codex or Claude Code connection.

native.modelsUnavailable: Editing and fetching a native connection’s models comes with native agent runs in a later version.
native.testUnavailable: Testing a native connection comes with native agent runs in a later version. Until then Orchester neither reaches its API nor reads its key, and profiles that use it cannot run.

secretMissing.title: A secret this server needs is archived or gone

mcp.removeInUse: Remove is unavailable while agent profiles choose this server: {{profiles}}.
mcp.detail: The agent’s CLI starts or reaches this server when an agent that gets it starts, and ends it with the agent. A server that does not start is listed in the run’s activity.
mcp.offDetail: Turned off: no agent gets this server. Profiles keep choosing it, and their agents get it again once it is turned on.

confirmRemove.title: Remove {{name}}?

account.manageDetail: Opens Settings › Accounts; this form keeps what you entered

apiProvider.label: Runs on
apiProvider.signInDetail: The CLI uses the account it is signed in to on this computer.
apiProvider.apiDetailClaude: Claude Code runs on an Anthropic-compatible API, such as DeepSeek’s, with an API key.
apiProvider.apiDetailCodex: Codex runs on an OpenAI Responses-compatible API, such as DeepSeek’s, with an API key.
apiProvider.interfaceClaude: Claude Code speaks the Anthropic Messages API: use the provider’s Anthropic-compatible address.
apiProvider.interfaceCodex: Codex speaks the OpenAI Responses API; a server that only speaks Chat Completions can’t run Codex.
apiProvider.keyHint: A project secret holds the key. Orchester gives it only to the CLI process it starts, which needs it to call the provider; the agent’s commands and MCP servers don’t get it. It is never shown, nor put in prompts or logs.
apiProvider.secretNameHint: Kept with the project’s secrets, in Development.
apiProvider.secretNameInvalid: Start with a capital letter and use capital letters, digits and underscores, such as DEEPSEEK_API_KEY.
apiProvider.secretNameTaken: Development already has a secret with this name; choose it above.
apiProvider.secretValueHint: Stored in this computer’s secret store when you save; it is not shown again.
apiProvider.modelsHint: The model ids the provider serves. Agent profiles on this connection choose from them.
apiProvider.sentTo: Prompts, repository content and command output are sent to {{host}}
apiProvider.sentToDetail: Under the provider’s terms and data policy, with this key. The MCP servers the CLI starts don’t get the key. Codex keeps variables whose names contain KEY, SECRET or TOKEN, the key among them, out of the commands the agent runs; Claude Code documents that it keeps variables whose names or values look like credentials out of them. Commands that need such a project variable, such as NPM_TOKEN or a DATABASE_URL with a password, fail on this connection.
apiProvider.notSupported: On an API provider Orchester reads no plan limits and counts tokens only where the provider reports them. The Orchestrator and auto mode’s reviewer don’t run on it.
apiProvider.sentToShort: Prompts, repository content and command output are sent to {{host}}, under its terms and data policy, with this key. Orchester reads no plan limits there.
apiProvider.interfaceClaudeShort: Claude Code speaks the Anthropic Messages API
apiProvider.interfaceCodexShort: Codex speaks the OpenAI Responses API
apiProvider.keyHintShort: A project secret holds it; only the CLI process gets it
apiProvider.modelsHintShort: The ids the provider serves; profiles choose from them

reasons.key: Choose the secret holding the API key, or New secret….
reasons.models: Enter at least one model the provider serves.

apiProvider.personOnly: Only a person saves a connection on an API provider here: input from an MCP client is taken only while you let automation change agent permissions.
apiProvider.checkFound: {{program}} {{version}} · runs on the API provider; its own sign-in is not used
apiProvider.nextStep: After saving, select this connection in an agent profile and choose one of its models.
apiProvider.keyArchived: Key secret missing: {{secret}} was archived. Choose a secret, or New secret….
apiProvider.planLimits: Not read on an API provider
apiProvider.detailConnected: The CLI answers. Orchester starts it on the API provider with the key from {{secret}}; the CLI’s own sign-in is not used.
apiProvider.detailKeyMissing: The key’s secret is archived or gone, so runs on this connection don’t start. Choose another secret in Edit connection, or restore it in Secrets.
apiProvider.offProvider: Saving takes {{name}} off the API provider
apiProvider.offProviderDetail: Its base URL and models are removed; agents start {{cli}} on the Default account’s sign-in. {{secret}} stays in Secrets.
apiProvider.offProviderDetailNoSecret: Its base URL and models are removed; agents start {{cli}} on the Default account’s sign-in.
